biological.citation: Single-cell profiling reveals immune disturbances landscape and HLA-F-mediated immune tolerance at the maternal-fetal interface in preeclampsia (PMID: 37854606)
biological.summary: Over-expression of HLA-F in Jar trophoblast cells promoted cell proliferation, invasion, and migration, while under-expression had the opposite effect. In NK-92MI cells, over-expression of HLA-F increased secretion of immunoregulatory cytokines CSF1 and CCL22 and promoted adaptive NKG2C+ NK cell transformation. HLA-F expression was confirmed reduced in preeclamptic placental decidua samples compared to controls by mIF staining.

biological.citation: HLA-F regulates the proliferation of trophoblast via PKM2-dependent glycolysis in the pathogenesis of preeclampsia (PMID: 40251569)
biological.summary: Over-expression of HLA-F in Jar trophoblast cells promoted proliferation and enhanced glycolysis by upregulating PKM2 protein expression and enzymatic activity; HLA-F was shown to bind the PKM gene promoter (via ChIP-seq) and reduce lactylation at PKM2 K305. Silencing PKM2 with siRNA abolished HLA-F-mediated glycolysis and proliferation, and a MiniPDX model confirmed that the PKM2 agonist TEPP-46 rescued proliferation in HLA-F-knockdown cells. HLA-F expression was reduced in extravillous trophoblast and villous cytotrophoblast from preeclampsia patients.

biological.citation: HLA Class Ib-receptor interactions during embryo implantation and early pregnancy (PMID: 35234898)
biological.summary: HLA-F is expressed in mid-secretory endometrium and fluctuates during the menstrual cycle, with high levels during the implantation window. HLA-F protein expression levels correlate with the number of CD56-positive NK cells in the mid-secretory endometrium. HLA-F and HLA-G SNP genotypes, including a SNP in a progesterone-responsive element, are associated with time-to-pregnancy and influence HLA-F expression levels.

biological.citation: Endometrial HLA-F expression is influenced by genotypes and correlates differently with immune cell infiltration in IVF and recurrent implantation failure patients (PMID: 35689445)
biological.summary: HLA-F protein is expressed in mid-secretory endometrium and its levels differ according to HLA-F SNP genotypes and diplotypes. Endometrial HLA-F was positively correlated with anti-inflammatory CD163+ M2 macrophage infiltration and CD56+ uNK cell abundance across the full cohort, though this relationship differed in recurrent implantation failure subgroups. HLA-F levels were negatively correlated with plasma progesterone in the female infertility RIF subgroup but positively correlated in the male infertility RIF subgroup.
biological.sample_size: 85 RIF women and 36 IVF control women

biological.citation: HLA-F transcriptional and protein differential expression according to its genetic polymorphisms (PMID: 37166140)
biological.summary: Three noncoding SNPs (rs1362126, rs2523405, and rs2523393) located in HLA-F-AS1 or upstream of HLA-F were confirmed to be associated with HLA-F mRNA and protein expression levels in PBMCs from healthy individuals, with the highest effect size and a double-dose effect. HLA-F mRNA is detected in most cell types, while the protein is localized in the ER and Golgi apparatus and reaches the cell membrane upon activation. HLA-F can be expressed as open conformers binding KIRs or as peptide-bound forms binding ILT2 and ILT4.
biological.sample_size: 1000 Genomes Project samples; healthy PBMC donors

biological.citation: Tetrameric complexes of HLA-E, HLA-F, and HLA-G (PMID: 12213342)
biological.summary: Tetrameric complexes of HLA-F were constructed and shown to bind to ILT2 (immunoglobulin-like transcript 2) and ILT4 receptors, identifying these as potential ligands/receptors for HLA-F. This parallels HLA-G tetramer interactions with ILT2 and ILT4, suggesting a shared receptor-binding mechanism among HLA class Ib molecules.

biological.citation: HLA-F and LILRB1 Genetic Polymorphisms Associated with Alloimmunisation in Sickle Cell Disease (PMID: 37686397)
biological.summary: Genetic polymorphisms in HLA-F and its receptor LILRB1 (located in their regulatory regions and associated with protein expression levels) were found to be associated with red blood cell alloimmunisation susceptibility in sickle cell disease patients. This suggests HLA-F participates in immune tolerance mechanisms relevant to transfusion alloimmunisation, analogous to its role in pregnancy tolerance.

biological.citation: HLA-F-AS1/miR-330-3p/PFN1 axis promotes colorectal cancer progression (PMID: 31863778)
biological.summary: The lncRNA HLA-F-AS1 (antisense RNA 1 of HLA-F) was significantly upregulated in colorectal cancer tissues and cell lines, and its overexpression promoted proliferation, migration, invasion, and blocked apoptosis of CRC cells. HLA-F-AS1 acts as a competing endogenous RNA by sponging miR-330-3p, thereby upregulating PFN1 expression and driving CRC progression. Knockdown of HLA-F-AS1 had the opposite tumor-suppressive effects.
biological.sample_size: CRC tissue samples and cell lines

biological.citation: HLA-E and HLA-F Are Overexpressed in Glioblastoma and HLA-E Increased After Exposure to Ionizing Radiation (PMID: 35181585)
biological.summary: HLA-F mRNA was significantly upregulated in glioblastoma (GBM) tissue samples compared to non-tumor brain tissue controls. Dysregulated HLA-F expression was also observed between patients with methylated versus unmethylated MGMT promoter status. These findings suggest HLA-F may contribute to immune escape in GBM and could serve as a diagnostic biomarker.
biological.sample_size: 69 GBM tissue samples and 21 non-tumor brain tissue controls

biological.citation: ASHG 2010 - Identification of multiple genetic variants related to nasopharyngeal carcinoma predisposition through genome-wide scan (W. Su et al.)
biological.summary: A genome-wide association study in a Taiwanese population identified significant associations between nasopharyngeal carcinoma (NPC) and two SNPs in HLA-F (rs3129055 and rs9258122; p = 7.36×10⁻¹¹ and 3.33×10⁻¹⁰, respectively). This represents the first GWAS report linking HLA-F genetic variants to NPC susceptibility, alongside HLA-A and GABBR1 associations on chromosome 6p21.3.
biological.sample_size: 277 NPC patients and 285 healthy controls, with independent replication sets
